newsitem.title: USA: White House's Tyson - exact level of NAIRU unclear.
newsitem.headline: White House's Tyson - exact level of NAIRU unclear.

text.p: White House economic adviser Laura Tyson on Tuesday said there has been an emerging consensus among economists that the level of U.S. unemployment that can incite inflationary pressures has fallen.
But there is no broad agreement on the new level for the non-accelerating inflation rate of unemployment (NAIRU), nor is there a consensus on the reasons for its decline, she said.

Speaking to a breakfast organized by Reuters, Tyson noted that previously many economists pegged the NAIRU at 6 percent but after the inflation rate has remained relatively steady even as the jobless rate has been below that level for the past two years, many experts now believe NAIRU is lower.

Tyson pointed to a number of theories put forth to explain the changing relationship between unemployment and inflation, including increased business competition that has made producers less likely to try to pass along price increases to consumers and new dynamics in the labor market that have made workers less likely to demand large wage increases.

Given the uncertainty surrounding the issue, Tyson said, "The correct thing to do at this point -- and that's what I think policy makers are doing -- is to try to learn more about the economy by observing its current behavior."
